hook: SCP-517 is an old fortune-telling machine with a grandmother puppet inside, its power cord cut and yet still working. The file is short and most of the horror happens offscreen, so take your time with the small printed fortunes collected at the end.
whyItMatters:
Much of the effect comes from pairing a homely, harmless-looking machine with an outcome that has never had a survivor. The most chilling details are procedural ones, like the exact minute of the attack and the list of places from which it has struck.

The fortunes give the machine a voice, a scolding and oddly affectionate one, and that voice makes a random curse sound like a verdict.
thingsToNotice: Anyone who wanders into the puppet's view gets a card, at most once an hour, and at 1:43 the next morning somewhere between ten and three dozen long, jointed arms come out of a low, dark, cramped spot such as a basement, a closet, an office vent, the space under a bed or a sewer grate. The target is dragged in and beaten until sunrise, anyone who interferes is pulled in as well, the remains are redacted, and nobody has survived. Remote cameras watching the likely exit points only caught arms reaching in from corners and off-frame until they filled the picture, and fragments of unidentified human DNA keep turning up where they appeared. The containment notes have been rewritten after an incident, with a ban on testing whose date has been struck through and moved from 1997 to 2002, and the dated fortunes run right up to that later year. Read in order, the cards sound like a grandmother passing judgment on wrongdoing, ending on a question about whether someone has been forgotten, though the article never says what any of its targets did.
